The problem

The conversation is happening now. Your next session is in three weeks.

  • The fight with your partner at 11pm, not at your Tuesday appointment
  • The raise you need to ask for tomorrow morning
  • The boundary with a parent you have never managed to set

So you walk in cold — and your first draft becomes the real thing.

Why the help you have does not fit

Help that knows you, or help that's actually there. Never both.

A therapist
Present, but scarce
A licensed human with real judgment. Expensive, booked weeks out, gone by the time the moment comes.
A chatbot
There, but typing
Available any time — in a text box. You can't rehearse a shaky voice, an interruption, or a silence in writing.
SILTAtherapy
The bridge
A phone call the second you need it. It plays the other person out loud, coaches you between takes — and is built to hand the human moments to a human.

The idea

You don't need advice. You need reps.

Call Mira and describe the scene. Mid-call, she becomes Alex — the person you're dreading — and pushes back the way you said they would. Say it badly. Press 1. Take the moment again.

Every hard conversation deserves a second draft.

Built on Guava

The whole thing is Guava primitives.

set_persona()
one call, two characters — Mira becomes Alex mid-conversation, new voice included
set_task() + Field()
the Expert's invented activity: objective, checklist, sensitive fields, completion criteria
on_action_request
the voice agent asks the Expert to replan — asynchronously, without dead air
on_dtmf
0 coach · 1 do-over · 9 end · * help — controls, not menus
on_escalate
drops the act, offers human support, never returns to fiction

This is the shipped adaptive.py, not slideware. Ten event handlers, one planner, no fixed flow.

adaptive.py · reasoner.py — excerpts
# the Expert rewrites the live call, mid-conversation
call.set_persona(
    organization_name="Second Draft",
    agent_name=scene.counterpart_name,  # "Alex"
    voice="jack",                       # Mira speaks "grace"
    agent_purpose=persona_prompt,       # scene = untrusted data
)
call.set_task(
    session.active_task,
    objective=activity.objective,       # invented live
    checklist=[guava.Say(announcement), *fields],
    completion_criteria="…no imposed turn count.",
)

# wiring: the same call, ten ways in
agent.on_caller_speech · on_action_request · on_dtmf
agent.on_escalate · on_task_complete · on_question …

# reasoner.py — decisions are typed and validated
response = generate(PLANNER_PROMPT + context.to_json(),
    json_schema=Decision.model_json_schema())

The part we refused to fake

Safety is code, not a disclaimer.

One-way doors
Crisis exits fiction
Crisis language stops the roleplay instantly. Safety mode has no path back to fiction — not by voice, not by keypad.
Consent, verified
Your words, not the model's
A new rehearsal needs the caller's own current words — the app itself checks the last utterance. A clear request or a yes to an offer counts; "maybe", hesitation, or a retraction blocks the scene.
Fail-closed keys
Unknown state? Ignore.
In safety mode the keypad goes dead — ending the call is the only key that still works. A state the router doesn't recognize ignores every key.
Nothing to leak
Private by construction
Telemetry disabled before the SDK loads, logs withhold transcripts, no conversation database, fields marked sensitive, callers asked to skip real names.
Honest limits
"This isn't therapy"
Mira says it in her greeting and the code means it: no diagnoses, no impersonating real people, and a phrase detector we call a backstop, not a clinician.

Act two

Tonight it's your coach. Next it's your therapist's.

Why it matters

One therapist. Ten times the care.

Timely
Help at 11pm, not in three weeks
The rehearsal happens when the fear is real — the night before, not the appointment after.
Leverage
The AI takes the reps
Human hours go where a human is needed. One practice covers many more people without burning out its clinicians.
Personal
Practice out loud, not in theory
Voice is the medium the fear lives in. You rehearse the shaky delivery, the pushback, the silence — the parts a text box can't hold.

The buyer is the practice. The dashboard is the product. The patients are why it spreads.

Why now

Voice
It finally holds character
Real-time, in-character, emotional conversation on a phone line is possible this year. It was not last year.
Platform
Guava made it a night's work
Personas, live task rewrites, escalation and DTMF on a real phone number — the hard telephony is primitives, so we spent tonight on the product.
Wedge
Regulated care wants this shape
A licensed human in the loop, safety in code, data that stays put. Exactly the room voice AI is allowed to enter first.
